title: Home and things
goal: Use 喺 correctly — before the verb for where an activity happens, after it for where something ends up — say what's there with 有, and describe where you live.
bekal: tell 喺 “to be at” apart from 喺 “at”
put the place phrase before the verb
use 住喺 for where you live
say there is / there isn't with 有 and 冇

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — Visiting Wong Lai's home
dialogs.intro: Andi has been invited to the Wong family's flat in Tai Kok Tsui. Watch where 喺 sits in each sentence — sometimes before the verb, sometimes after, and the rule is not random.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [入嚟啦|Jap6 lei4 laa1]！[唔好客氣|M4 hou2 haak3 hei3]。
lines.id: Come in, come in! Make yourself at home.
lines.literal: enter — come — go-on. don't — guest — air.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [打攪晒|Daa2 gaau2 saai3]。[你哋住喺幾樓呀|Nei5 dei6 zyu6 hai2 gei2 lau2 aa3]？
lines.id: Sorry to trouble you. What floor do you live on?
lines.literal: hit — disturb — completely. you-all — live — at — which — floor — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [十八樓|Sap6 baat3 lau2]。[部電梯|Bou6 din6 tai1][有時壞㗎|jau5 si4 waai6 gaa3]。
lines.id: The eighteenth. The lift sometimes breaks down.
lines.literal: ten — eight — floor. classifier — electric — ladder — have — time — broken — emphasis.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [間屋好靚喎|Gaan1 uk1 hou2 leng3 wo3]！[有幾多間房呀|Jau5 gei2 do1 gaan1 fong2 aa3]？
lines.id: Your place is lovely! How many rooms are there?
lines.literal: classifier — house — filler — pretty — you-know. have — how — many — classifier — room — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [兩間|Loeng5 gaan1]。[我同細佬一間|Ngo5 tung4 sai3 lou2 jat1 gaan1]，[爸媽一間|baa4 maa1 jat1 gaan1]。
lines.id: Two. My little brother and I share one, Mom and Dad have the other.
lines.literal: two — classifier. I — with — younger-brother — one — classifier, dad — mom — one — classifier.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [廁所喺邊度呀|Ci3 so2 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
lines.id: Where's the toilet?
lines.literal: toilet — at — which — place — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [喺廚房隔籬|Hai2 cyu4 fong2 gaak3 lei4]。[門後面嗰度|Mun4 hau6 min6 go2 dou6]。
lines.id: Next to the kitchen. Behind that door.
lines.literal: at — kitchen — next-door. door — back — side — that — place.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [你哋喺呢度住咗幾耐呀|Nei5 dei6 hai2 ni1 dou6 zyu6 zo2 gei2 noi6 aa3]？
lines.id: How long have you lived here?
lines.literal: you-all — at — this — place — live — already — how — long — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [十年喇|Sap6 nin4 laa3]。[細但係好方便|Sai3 daan6 hai6 hou2 fong1 bin6]，[樓下就係街市|lau4 haa6 zau6 hai6 gaai1 si5]。
lines.id: Ten years. It's small but handy — the market is right downstairs.
lines.literal: ten — year — already. small — but — filler — handy, floor — below — just — is — market.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我間房冇窗|Ngo5 gaan1 fong2 mou5 coeng1]，[所以好焗|so2 ji5 hou2 guk6]。
lines.id: My room has no window, so it's really stuffy.
lines.literal: I — classifier — room — not-have — window, so — filler — stuffy.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [有冇冷氣呀|Jau5 mou5 laang5 hei3 aa3]？
lines.id: Is there air conditioning?
lines.literal: have — not-have — cold — air — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [有|Jau5]，[但係開親就好嘈|daan6 hai6 hoi1 can1 zau6 hou2 cou4]。
lines.id: Yes, but every time I turn it on it's really noisy.
lines.literal: have, but — open — each-time — then — filler — noisy.

notes: **[打攪晒|Daa2 gaau2 saai3] = “sorry to trouble you”, said as you step into someone's home.** The host replies [唔使客氣|M4 sai2 haak3 hei3] or [唔好客氣|M4 hou2 haak3 hei3]. 🇭🇰 This is a set exchange; saying it straight away makes you sound like you know the customs.

**[樓|lau2] means both “floor” and “building”.** [十八樓|sap6 baat3 lau2] = 18th floor; [樓下|lau4 haa6] = downstairs; [樓上|lau4 soeng6] = upstairs. ⚠️ Note the tone change: in 樓下 and 樓上 it's read *lau4*, but as “the Nth floor” it's *lau2*.
**[間|gaan1] is the classifier for enclosed spaces**: houses, rooms, shops, schools. [一間屋|jat1 gaan1 uk1] = a house; [三間房|saam1 gaan1 fong2] = three rooms.
🇭🇰 **Floor 4 is often skipped in Hong Kong buildings**, because [四|sei3] sounds like [死|sei2] (die). In some buildings the lift buttons jump from 3 to 5, and floor 13 sometimes goes missing too.
**[方便|fong1 bin6] = handy, easy to get to.** It's the word Hong Kongers use most to praise a home — more often than praising its size, since space is a rare luxury.
**[焗|guk6] = stuffy, hot with no air moving.** A native Cantonese word with no one-word equivalent in English or Mandarin. [好焗|hou2 guk6] is the summer complaint you'll hear most.

**[開親|hoi1 can1] = “every time it's turned on”.** [親|can1] after a verb means “every time … always …”. [食親都肚痛|Sik6 can1 dou1 tou5 tung3] = every time I eat, I get a stomachache. A very Cantonese pattern that doesn't exist in Mandarin.

grammars.title: 喺 — two positions, two meanings
body: [喺|hai2] has two roles, and what decides its meaning is **where it stands relative to the verb**. This is the most important point in the whole unit.

head: Role
Pattern
Example
Meaning
rows: [我喺屋企食飯|Ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6]。
[我住喺旺角|Ngo5 zyu6 hai2 Wong6 gok3]。
[本書放喺枱面|Bun2 syu1 fong3 hai2 toi2 min2]。
The book is put on the table.

after: ⚠️ **The rule: if the place is just the setting of an activity, 喺 goes BEFORE the verb.** [我喺公司返工|Ngo5 hai2 gung1 si1 faan1 gung1] = I work at the office. 我返工喺公司 is wrong.

**If the action itself RESULTS in being at that place, 喺 goes AFTER.** The list of such verbs is short: [住|zyu6] (live), [坐|co5] (sit), [企|kei5] (stand), [放|fong3] (put), [擺|baai2] (place), [瞓|fan3] (lie down). Memorize these six as the exceptions.
⚠️ **Don't mix it up with [係|hai6].** [我係老師|Ngo5 hai6 lou5 si1] = I'm a teacher. [我喺學校|Ngo5 hai2 hok6 haau6] = I'm at school. Same letters, one tone apart, two very different sentences.
**[喺度|hai2 dou6] = “is here / is there”**, often used on its own: [佢喺唔喺度呀|Keoi5 hai2 m4 hai2 dou6 aa3]？ = is he in? You'll use this every time you call an office.

grammars.title: 有 for existence: place + 有 + thing
body: To say “there is something somewhere”, Cantonese puts **the place first**, then 有, then the thing. The reverse of English “there is … in …”.

head: Cantonese
Meaning
rows: [屋企有兩間房|Uk1 kei2 jau5 loeng5 gaan1 fong2]。
There are two rooms at home.
[樓下有街市|Lau4 haa6 jau5 gaai1 si5]。
[我間房冇窗|Ngo5 gaan1 fong2 mou5 coeng1]。
[附近有冇便利店呀|Fu6 gan6 jau5 mou5 bin6 lei6 dim3 aa3]？
Is there a convenience store nearby?
[枱上面有本書|Toi2 soeng6 min6 jau5 bun2 syu1]。
There's a book on the table.
[廁所入面有人|Ci3 so2 jap6 min6 jau5 jan4]。

after: **Compare these two sentences — both are correct but they mean different things:** [枱上面有本書|Toi2 soeng6 min6 jau5 bun2 syu1] = there's a book on the table (introducing it). [本書喺枱上面|Bun2 syu1 hai2 toi2 soeng6 min6] = the book is on the table (we already know which book).
**The general rule: something NEW takes 有; something ALREADY known takes 喺.** This does the job that the articles *a* and *the* do in English.

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Looking for a place to live
dialogs.intro: Andi calls a property agent. Renting talk in Hong Kong is full of numbers and shorthand — and you already have almost all of it from earlier units.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [喂|Wai2]，[你好|nei5 hou2]。[我想租樓|Ngo5 soeng2 zou1 lau2]。
lines.id: Hello, good afternoon. I'd like to rent a place.
lines.literal: hello, you — good. I — want — rent — building.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [你想住喺邊區呀|Nei5 soeng2 zyu6 hai2 bin1 keoi1 aa3]？
lines.id: Which area do you want to live in?
lines.literal: you — want — live — at — which — district — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [旺角附近|Wong6 gok3 fu6 gan6]，[因為我喺嗰度返工|jan1 wai6 ngo5 hai2 go2 dou6 faan1 gung1]。
lines.id: Near Mongkok, because I work there.
lines.literal: Mongkok — near, because — I — at — that — place — return — work.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [要幾大呀|Jiu3 gei2 daai6 aa3]？[幾多呎|Gei2 do1 cek3]？
lines.id: How big? How many square feet?
lines.literal: need — how — big — huh. how — many — feet.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我一個人住|Ngo5 jat1 go3 jan4 zyu6]，[一間房夠喇|jat1 gaan1 fong2 gau3 laa3]。
lines.id: I live alone, so one room is enough.
lines.literal: I — one — classifier — person — live, one — classifier — room — enough — already.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [租金預算幾多呀|Zou1 gam1 jyu6 syun3 gei2 do1 aa3]？
lines.id: What's your rent budget?
lines.literal: rent — money — pre — calculate — how — much — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [一萬蚊以下|Jat1 maan6 man1 ji5 haa6]。[有冇呀|Jau5 mou5 aa3]？
lines.id: Under ten thousand. Do you have anything?
lines.literal: one — ten-thousand — dollar — from — below. have — not-have — huh.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [有|Jau5]，[但係好細|daan6 hai6 hou2 sai3]，[大概二百呎|daai6 koi3 ji6 baak3 cek3]。
lines.id: Yes, but it's very small, about two hundred square feet.
lines.literal: have, but — filler — small, rough — approximate — two — hundred — feet.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [有冇窗㗎|Jau5 mou5 coeng1 gaa3]？[有冇冷氣|Jau5 mou5 laang5 hei3]？
lines.id: Does it have a window? Air conditioning?
lines.literal: have — not-have — window — emphasis. have — not-have — cold — air.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [兩樣都有|Loeng5 joeng6 dou1 jau5]。[仲有洗衣機|Zung6 jau5 sai2 ji1 gei1]。
lines.id: It has both. There's a washing machine too.
lines.literal: two — kind — all — have. still — have — wash — clothes — machine.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [咁我想睇下|Gam2 ngo5 soeng2 tai2 haa5]。[聽日得唔得呀|Ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3]？
lines.id: Then I'd like to see it. Is tomorrow OK?
lines.literal: then — I — want — look — a-bit. tomorrow — can — not — can — huh.

lines.speaker: 經紀:
lines.text: [得|Dak1]。[聽日三點|Ting1 jat6 saam1 dim2]，[喺地鐵站B出口等|hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 B ceot1 hau2 dang2]。
lines.id: Sure. Tomorrow at three, wait at exit B of the MTR station.
lines.literal: can. tomorrow — three — o'clock, at — MTR — station — B — exit — mouth — wait.

notes: **[喂|Wai2] is “hello” on the phone, and ONLY on the phone.** ⚠️ It must be tone 2 (rising). Said with tone 6 (*wai6*), it becomes a rude “hey!”. 🔁 The full phone vocabulary is in Unit 10.
**[租樓|zou1 lau2] = to rent a place to live.** [租|zou1] means both to rent and to rent out; who's doing it tells you which. [業主|jip6 zyu2] = owner; [租客|zou1 haak3] = tenant; [租金|zou1 gam1] = rent.

🇭🇰 **Home sizes in Hong Kong are measured in [呎|cek3], square feet** — not square meters. 200 呎 is roughly 18.5 m². That's not a typo: a flat that small is normal, and it's called a [劏房|tong1 fong2] if it's carved out of a bigger flat.
**[區|keoi1] = district, area.** [邊區|bin1 keoi1]？ = which area? Hong Kong is divided into eighteen 區, and people give their address by district more often than by street name.

**[因為|jan1 wai6] = because, and it goes before the reason.** Its partner is [所以|so2 ji5] (so). ⚠️ Unlike English, Cantonese can use both in one sentence: [因為落雨，所以唔去|Jan1 wai6 lok6 jyu5, so2 ji5 m4 heoi3] = because it's raining, (so) I'm not going.
**[以下|ji5 haa6] = under (a number), [以上|ji5 soeng6] = over.** Both come **after** the number: [一萬蚊以下|jat1 maan6 man1 ji5 haa6] = under ten thousand dollars.
**[兩樣都有|Loeng5 joeng6 dou1 jau5] = “it has both”.** Remember 都 from Unit 1: with a plural subject it means “all”. [兩個都得|Loeng5 go3 dou1 dak1] = either one is fine.

grammars.title: Describing nouns: description + 嘅 + noun
body: To describe a noun, Cantonese puts the description **in front**, linked with [嘅|ge3]. Short adjectives come first in English too, but longer phrases (“the house in Mongkok”) come after — in Cantonese they all go before.

head: Cantonese
Meaning
Literal
rows: [新買嘅電話|san1 maai5 ge3 din6 waa2]
[喺旺角嘅屋|hai2 Wong6 gok3 ge3 uk1]

after: **[嘅|ge3] can be dropped when the description is one syllable and fused with the noun**: [新屋|san1 uk1] (new house), [大房|daai6 fong2] (big room). If the description is longer, 嘅 is required.
🇭🇰 **[嘅|ge3] also stands in for the noun itself when it's obvious**: [呢個係我嘅|Ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 ge3] = this one is mine. [平嘅有冇呀|Peng4 ge3 jau5 mou5 aa3]？ = do you have a cheap one?
⚠️ **Don't use Mandarin 的.** The character is different, the sound is different, and in Hong Kong 的 only shows up in formal writing.

sections.title: The home and what's in it

blocks.title: Three things about Hong Kong homes
items: 🇭🇰 **Shoes come off at the door**, and your host will hand you [拖鞋|to1 haai2]. If they don't, ask [使唔使除鞋呀|Sai2 m4 sai2 ceoi4 haai4 aa3]？

**[冷氣|laang5 hei3] is the everyday word for air conditioning**, literally “cold air”. [開冷氣|hoi1 laang5 hei3] = turn on the AC; [熄冷氣|sik1 laang5 hei3] = turn it off. [開|hoi1] and [熄|sik1] work for every electrical appliance.

**A [劏房|tong1 fong2] is a flat cut up into several tiny units.** [劏|tong1] literally means “to slaughter, slice open” — an honest term, and one you'll often hear on the news. For newcomers on a small budget, this is what gets offered most.

blocks.text: The question-and-answer pattern below looks trivial, but it's the densest 喺 practice in the whole module. Do all of it out loud.

head: Question
Answer
rows: [我嘅電話喺邊度呀|Ngo5 ge3 din6 waa2 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
[鎖匙喺邊度呀|So2 si4 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
[喺個袋入面|Hai2 go3 doi2 jap6 min6]。
[廁所喺邊度呀|Ci3 so2 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
[喺廚房隔籬|Hai2 cyu4 fong2 gaak3 lei4]。
[佢喺唔喺度呀|Keoi5 hai2 m4 hai2 dou6 aa3]？
[附近有冇便利店呀|Fu6 gan6 jau5 mou5 bin6 lei6 dim3 aa3]？
[你住喺邊度呀|Nei5 zyu6 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
[我住喺旺角|Ngo5 zyu6 hai2 Wong6 gok3]。

blocks.title: Four handy household sentences
items: [唔該開燈|M4 goi1 hoi1 dang1]。 — Please turn on the light.
[熄咗冷氣佢|Sik1 zo2 laang5 hei3 keoi5]。 — Turn off the AC. (Note the 佢 at the end: it points back to the thing, a very Cantonese habit.)
[部電梯壞咗|Bou6 din6 tai1 waai6 zo2]。 — The lift is broken.
[我唔記得帶鎖匙|Ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 so2 si4]。 — I forgot to bring my keys.

exercises.prompt: Correct these wrong sentences, then write the right version in Jyutping.
items: [我住旺角|Ngo5 zyu6 Wong6 gok3]。
[我食飯喺屋企|Ngo5 sik6 faan6 hai2 uk1 kei2]。
[我係屋企|Ngo5 hai6 uk1 kei2]。
[有兩間房喺屋企|Jau5 loeng5 gaan1 fong2 hai2 uk1 kei2]。
[我的房好細|Ngo5 dik1 fong2 hou2 sai3]。

answers: 係 — 喺 — 喺 — 係 — 喺 … 喺 — 喺
我喺屋企食飯。 — 我住喺旺角。 — 佢喺中環返工。 — 本書放喺枱上面。 — 我哋喺地鐵站等。
你哋 住 喺 幾 樓 呀 — 屋企 有 兩 間 房 — 我 間 房 冇 窗 — 附近 有冇 便利店 呀 — 喺 廚房 隔籬 — 因為 落雨 所以 唔 去
I live in Mongkok; the market is right downstairs. — The flat is very small, but it's handy. — The lift is broken. — My keys are in the bag. — Every time the AC is on, it's really noisy.
Ngo5 zyu6 hai2 Wong6 gok3. — Ngo5 gaan1 fong2 mou5 coeng1. — Uk1 kei2 jau5 loeng5 gaan1 fong2. — Ci3 so2 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3? — Ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6.
Ngo5 zyu6 hai2 Wong6 gok3. — Ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6. — Ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2. — Uk1 kei2 jau5 loeng5 gaan1 fong2. — Ngo5 gaan1 fong2 hou2 sai3.
wave: Five minutes before Unit 8: stand in the middle of the room you're reading in and name the location of ten things around you out loud — [本書喺枱上面|Bun2 syu1 hai2 toi2 soeng6 min6]、[個袋喺櫈下面|Go3 doi2 hai2 dang3 haa6 min6]. Then describe where you live in four sentences: which floor, how many rooms, what's downstairs, and whether it's 方便. That's all of Unit 7 in one paragraph.
